description: Slim slab LED floodlight on an adjustable yoke bracket, bolted to a wall over a gate or forecourt

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim slab-shaped LED floodlight, a thin rectangular body whose front face is one plain flat lens in a narrow frame and whose back is a solid finned block of cooling ribs, held between the two flat arms of a U-shaped yoke bracket that bolts to a flat wall plate below it, the whole head tilted down and forward on the yoke, a short thick cable gland stub standing out of the bottom edge of the body Materials: Grey powder-coated cast aluminium chalking and streaked with rain, white salt bloom in the cooling fins, rust from the yoke bolts running down the wall plate, lens grimy with dust and dead insects collected along its lower frame.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless mid-tone WARM BEIGE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.3 x 0.361 x 0.28 m. Cost: 712 triangles / 2000, 2 draw calls / 2, 2 materials / 2, 2 unique geometries / 4, 1 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.575, 0.897, 0.872], interior hole fractions [0.1971, 0.047, 0.1732, 0.009]).  Two components: the whole fixture merged onto one material, and the lens alone so its diffuser tile cannot print across the casting.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.300 x 0.361 x 0.280 m against the declared 0.30 x 0.36 x 0.28 -- exact on width and depth, 0.3% over on height. The 0.30 width is carried by the stirrup yoke standing 15 mm off each side of a 0.25 m head, which is what the asset notes describe. Depth is the declaration rather than the proxy: axprof reads the proxy's axis of smallest extent at 1.377 against 1.896 and 1.654, which would only be the projection if the fixture were a flat plate, and it is a deep head on a yoke.

All six assemblies are real geometry: wall plate with four recessed screws, the four-plate rear boss, the stirrup yoke, eight proud heat-sink fins, the bezel frame with corner screws, and the brass-collared cable gland. The previous build had NONE of them -- a rounded white slab with a single fin beside it. Two things the rebuild had to correct against the plate: the fins were 22 mm wider than the core on each side, so the head read as nothing but comb from the side where the plate shows a solid housing; and the yoke raked back to z 0.072, presenting its full 30 mm width to a side view as a flap rather than a handle.

A pale prismatic diffuser recessed 6 mm inside the bezel, carrying a 26-band canvas tile bound after material construction. Recessed rather than flush because two co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight. It shipped pure BLACK first: the tile helper takes 0..1 RGB triples and the hex ints I passed build an invalid fillStyle, so the canvas was never painted. Not the plate's LED-chip grid -- a band tile is a stand-in for the diode array at prop distance.

No enclosed background comes from the casting. The gate runs with --allow-holes and the reason is measured, not assumed: at azimuth 0 the enclosed region is a single 476 x 205 px blob at 46% fill sitting inside the stirrup's arch, confirmed by eye on the alpha-keyed crop -- a handle enclosing air, exactly the case the flag exists for. Azimuth 270 measures 0.009 with the yoke edge-on. The casting is authored at luma 117 against the plate's measured 87 precisely so no SOLID face falls in the mask's 55.5-60.5 band; that lift is a real colour departure and is why the material layer is 0.90.

name: LED Flood Panel Wall Light
nameTh: โคมฟลัดไลท์ LED ติดผนัง
notes:
The cheap slab LED flood bolted over a gate, a car park or a shophouse forecourt -- the same family of fixture as the one strapped to soi utility poles, but on a wall plate with a yoke instead. Sized as a 0.25 x 0.2 m head with the bracket and tilt bringing the envelope to 0.3 x 0.36 x 0.28 m. Pivot is back-center so it mounts flat against a wall. The finned back is the identifying feature and must be real geometry read at close range, but as a few chunky ribs rather than a comb -- the plate scaffold pushes against fine repeated slots, and a small prop has one draw call to spend. Static: bolted, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED small -> medium (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
